title: Welcome: How This Course Works
objectives: How a lesson actually works, start to finish
Where to find the tour, the glossary, and hints
Why none of this can cost you money

steps.title: Welcome to Rekt School
steps.body:
Five minutes before you touch anything.

Every lesson is a short loop. You read one idea, watch it happen in the panel next to you, answer two questions, then get links to the real product. Same loop every time:

- **Read** - one idea, in plain English
- **Deep dive** - the mechanics underneath, if you want them
- **Quiz** - two questions, Aura points on the line
- **Explore** - the actual product, not a diagram of it

A couple of lessons open with a tour of the page instead. This one does.

**Maxi** is the voice you'll hear along the way. Maxi is a character we wrote for the course - no real person behind it, no wallet, no bag to defend. When a number on screen doesn't make sense, hit **Hint** and Maxi explains that specific number, not the textbook version of it.

**Why none of this can cost you money**

Everything runs on **Solana Devnet**. That's a public test network running the same software as mainnet, with none of the money. The SOL you spend comes out of a faucet - no market for it, nothing to sell, nobody cares if you burn it.

So you'll connect a real <Term id="wallet">wallet</Term>, sign real <Term id="transaction">transactions</Term>, and watch them land on-chain. You'll also do it wrong at some point. The cost of wrong here is the ten seconds you spend reading the error.

Simply put: the mechanics are identical to mainnet, and the bill isn't there.

By the end of Tier 1 you'll be able to open any wallet's history and tell what happened, decide whether a token is safe to touch, follow where a <Term id="gas_fee">gas fee</Term> went, and recognise the pattern before a scam drains a fresh wallet.

steps.title: A quick tour of this page
Which network you're on
steps.text: Says which network the page is talking to. Lessons never touch mainnet - the money comes from a faucet, so signing something you don't fully understand costs you nothing.

steps.title: Your Aura
steps.text: Your score. Quiz question right, it goes up. Wrong, it goes down. On-chain tasks pay in the same way.

steps.title: The reading side
steps.text: The current step and the explanation for it. Nothing here is timed - take as long as you want.

steps.title: The doing side
steps.text: Simulators and real on-chain transactions, results the moment you act. On your phone this sits behind the Practice tab.

steps.title: If you get stuck
steps.text: Maxi gives you one clue at a time. The first is a nudge, not the answer.

steps.title: Here, mistakes are reversible
steps.body:
On mainnet the first time you set slippage too wide, it comes straight out of your balance. No refund, no support desk, no partial undo.

The order we use is: **do it, see what the chain actually did, then do it again.**

A trade that fails in the simulator isn't a mark against you. It's the cheapest version of that mistake you'll ever get, and nobody's balance here is moving. So break things on purpose.

steps.title: What actually happens when you press a button
steps.body:
The site doesn't touch your money. It can't.

What happens instead: the site writes up an unsigned transaction - swap this for that, send here - and hands it to your <Term id="wallet">wallet</Term>. Your wallet shows you the details. You approve. The wallet signs it with your private key and sends it to the validators.

The key never leaves your extension. Only the signature goes out, and the signature is public. Anyone can verify that you approved exactly this transaction without ever seeing how you approved it.

That's the whole trust model, and it's why nobody at Rekt School can move your funds even if they wanted to.

questions.prompt: What kind of money is used in Rekt School lessons?
options: Real US Dollars from your bank account
Free Solana Devnet tokens issued from a faucet
questions.explainRight: Right - Devnet SOL comes out of a faucet. No market for it, nothing to lose.
questions.explainWrong: No. Lessons run on Devnet, where the SOL and the gas come out of a faucet. None of it has value.

questions.prompt: Does the Rekt School website ever hold your private key or seed phrase?
options: Yes, it stores them in an encrypted database
No. Your private key stays inside your wallet and the site never sees it
Yes, but only when you click 'Swap'
Yes, to pay for your gas fees
questions.explainRight: That's it. The site prepares the transaction, you sign it in your wallet, the key never moves.
questions.explainWrong: It can't. Non-custodial apps are built so they never see your key - and a site asking for your seed phrase is a drainer, not a wallet.
